what_happened: The job "Add scope-guard running-line watcher: flags, pauses, status display" (20261026-015419-4j37) failed in planning, before any code was written. After round 3 of 3 the critic still said the plan needed revising. The critic confirmed the named code exists (group_lines, RequestRecord, evaluate_before_attempt, the run.rs Finished arm and dispatch, Athena::retry). It also agreed the design is sound: hook go and dispatch, make retry refuse, and test through the fixture. Two major findings remained. (1) The criterion 6 never-kills demonstration runs go on a Dispatched job, but go always refuses that state, and the registry check passes trivially. (2) The plan passes p90 = 0.0, but t3_cost only pauses when p90 > 0, so the criterion 5 T3 pause test cannot reach a pause. There were two minor findings. reading.rs is not among the reading's deliverables. The plan does not say how the third linked request is made when retry refuses, or how dispatch finds the line head of a new request. The event lists no unmet acceptance criteria and no failed checks. Nothing was delivered.
cause: The planning stage writes demonstrations without running them against the real guards and thresholds in the code. It did not check that the state it sets up (a Dispatched job, p90 = 0.0) is accepted by the function under test. A demonstration that sets up an impossible state, or passes trivially, looks fine until the critic traces the code. The critic is the first stage to do that tracing. It gets only three rounds and keeps no partial plan, so a gap found in the last round fails the job. The reading also left out a file the design needs (reading.rs), which cost a round on a minor finding. Nothing requires a plan to name, for each demonstration, the precondition guard it passes through and a control that fails without the behavior.
prevention: Give the planning stage a required step for each criterion's demonstration. It must name the entry function, quote the state guards and thresholds on the path (such as go refusing Dispatched, or t3_cost needing p90 > 0), and show that the setup state and inputs get past them. It must also include a control that fails when the behavior is removed. The critic should check this table first, in round 1, instead of finding the gaps late. The stage should also derive the touched-file list from the plan and add any missing files (such as reading.rs) to the deliverables before round 1.
proposed_request: Add the scope-guard running-line watcher: it flags and pauses a request's line when its running cost passes the guard thresholds, and the status display shows the flag and pause. Hook the watcher into go and dispatch. Make retry refuse a paused line. Deliverables include crates/athena-core/src/scope_guard.rs, run.rs, status display code and the single-call edit in crates/athena-core/src/reading.rs. Acceptance: (1) a flagged line shows as flagged in status; (2) a third linked request on a flagged line is refused, and the test says how that request is made given that retry refuses; (3) dispatch finds the line head of a new request, and the plan says how; (4) the T3 pause fires when p90 is greater than 0, shown by a test that passes a real positive p90 and fails if the pause is removed; (5) a pause never kills a running job, shown by a test that starts from a state go accepts (not Dispatched) and fails if the guard is removed; (6) for each demonstration, the plan names the guard conditions on its path and shows the setup passes them. Run the normal repo checks and add a changelog entry.
